course_subtitle: Follow an OCP contribution from initial submission through review, approval, and publication.
course_description_html:
This course guides contributors through the OCP contribution process, from initiating a submission and working in the contribution platform through review, approval, and publication. You’ll learn the responsibilities of contributors, Project Leads, Steering Committee representatives, and OCP Foundation staff at each stage.


Click START COURSE or select a lesson below.

blocks.heading_html: Welcome to the OCP Contribution Process!

blocks.body_html:
This module aims to provide new contributors with a comprehensive guide on how to submit their work and get it published within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community.

The OCP Contribution Process is a structured workflow, managed through the Contribution Hub that guides you, the contributor, through every step of getting your work published within the OCP Database. Our goal is to make this process transparent and straightforward, with clear expectations for what you'll encounter and what actions you'll need to take.

blocks.body_html:
The full process can be as quick as 8 weeks, but may extend to 12 weeks (or more) depending on meeting schedules and how quickly you can prepare your documentation.

Whether you're submitting for the first time or you're an experienced member of our community, sharing a new specification, white paper, or software contribution, this module will walk you through the entire process.
By the end of this module, you will be able to:

items_html: Kick off your contribution in the OCP workflow tool.
Sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA).
Collaborate with Project Leads and the Steering Committee Representative.

blocks.body_html: Estimated time to complete: 15 minutes.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.body_html: The OCP Contribution Process is broadly divided into three main phases:

items_html: Review and Document Preparation
Approval and Publication

blocks.body_html:
The entire workflow is managed through the OCP Contribution Hub. This tool streamlines your contribution journey from the idea to publication, ensuring all necessary reviews and approvals are secured.

Every submission is reviewed and approved by the Project Lead(s) and SC Rep, automatically assigned based on the Project and Contribution Type selected when submitting the Start Your Contribution form.

Click each card to learn who they are and what they do.

back.description_html:
Project Lead (PL)

The Project Lead reviews your abstract, schedules the Project presentation, and reviews your final draft for acceptance to the Steering Committee Rep.

Steering Committee Representative (SC Rep)

The Steering Committee Representative for your project confirms that your contribution is ready for presentation to an upcoming OCP Steering Committee Meeting. The Steering Committee reviews your contribution and holds a vote, requiring a majority for publication eligibility.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html: Understanding the Platform

blocks.body_html:
Your contribution journey takes place in your dedicated workspace on the Contribution Hub. Here, you'll track your submission progress, communicate with reviewers, and upload your documents.

Let's explore the platform.
Click the info markers to learn about each feature.

items.title: Flow Tab
items.description_html: This is the main tab in your workspace, displaying the Contribution Process steps in their respective boxes.

items.title: Files Tab
items.description_html: This tab shows all the files you have submitted to this Contribution Process. If you need to delete a file you uploaded by mistake, you can do that here.

items.title: Chat Window
items.description_html:
This is a two-way communication window with your Project Lead, SC Rep and OCP Foundation Staff.

It is used to ask questions, seek clarification, or report any issues. You can also upload supplemental documents here, if needed. Additionally, this window displays notifications for the completed steps.

*If you decide to withdraw your submission, you must communicate this through the Chat Window.

items.title: Contribution Steps
items.description_html: Each box is a step in the Contribution Process, representing the main workflow from start to finish. Steps unlock as each participant completes their assigned task.

items.title: Green Buttons
items.description_html: A green button on the right side of a step means you need to complete it. Once completed, the workflow will advance to the next step in the process. If you do not see a green button, that action is assigned to another participant in the workflow.

items.title: Profile Icons
items.description_html:
Next to each step, you will see profile icons that indicate whose responsibility it is to complete that step.

If your profile icon is present, you are responsible for completing the step. If the Project Lead's, SC Rep's or OCP Foundation Staff's profile icon is displayed, they are responsible for completing the step, and no action is required from you.

If there are more than one profile icons present, the step involves both you and other participants (for example, you might upload a document, and the Project Lead reviews and approves it).

blocks.body_html: You can access your personal dashboard by clicking Back to Dashboard in the top left corner of the platform. It provides an overview of:

items_html: Your contact at the OCP Foundation.
Your current open contributions.
Any meetings that have been scheduled within the tool.
Quick links to helpful OCP resources.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html: Contribution Types

blocks.body_html:
Here are four common contribution types that can be published on the OCP Contribution Database.

Click the ‘+’ icons to learn more about each.

items.title: Specifications
items.description_html:
• Specifications define architectural frameworks (hardware, software, networking, etc.). 

  • Templates are available to structure your documentation.

  • Submissions require a contribution license agreement (CLA), engagement with an OCP Project, and presentations to both the Project and Steering Committee.

items.title: Whitepaper / Documents
items.description_html:
• Typically, case studies, guidelines, and best practices.

  • Submissions require an abstract for approval, and use of the OCP Documents template.

  • Often published using a Creative Commons License.

items.title: Design Files
items.description_html:
• These are design-specific assets based on published specifications.

  • Submissions require a CLA, and presentations to both the Project and Steering Committee.

items.title: Software
items.description_html:
• Can include software code, testing, documentation, and bug fixes.

  • Submissions go to OCP’s GitHub Repository and follow a process similar to specifications, including the use of an open license, and require presentations to both the Project and Steering Committee.

blocks.body_html:
This training module will walk you through a specification contribution; other contribution types follow a similar flow but have fewer steps. Understanding the specification process will help prepare you for the submission of all contribution types.

The contribution process remains broadly the same regardless of which project you select. You may be requested to make changes to the content specific to your contribution.
You can submit as many contributions as you like, and they can be in progress at the same time.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html: Contribution Form

blocks.body_html: Your OCP contribution journey begins by submitting the Start a New Contribution form, available in the Contributions section of the OCP website. It asks for key details about your submission, such as the type of contribution and a brief description of your proposed work.

Once you submit the form, it automatically triggers the creation of your personalized workflow within the OCP Contribution Hub. Almost immediately, you'll receive a Welcome email from OCP. Inside that email, click the Join Workspace button. This will direct you to your dedicated workspace on the platform.

This workspace is a central hub for the rest of the process. It’s where you'll track your submission's progress, communicate with reviewers, and upload required documentation.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 1
Provide an abstract to the Project Lead(s)

blocks.body_html:
To begin, click the Review button on the far right of Step 1. This opens a side panel that prompts you to submit your abstract. Select Fill Out Form, and a new window will appear where you'll be asked to enter a contribution title and a brief abstract. You can either save your progress and return later or hit Submit when ready.

Once you submit your abstract, Step 1 is complete.

Click the play icon to see it in action.

This step is essential. The Project Lead (PL) assigned to your submission will evaluate your abstract and decide whether it meets the criteria to proceed.

Project Leads typically review abstracts within a few business days.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 2
Sign CLA

blocks.body_html:
While waiting for the PL to approve your abstract, you can complete Step 2.

In this step, you'll sign the Contributor License Agreement (CLA). This legal agreement confirms that you, and anyone else involved, give OCP the necessary rights to publish and share your work.

If there are multiple contributors, you'll also indicate how many and provide the contact information for any authorized signers.
Signing a CLA does not mean that you are giving up your company's Intellectual Property (IP).
Click Review on the far right of Step 2.
In the side panel, select Sign.
A new window will open, prompting you to enter your full name, initials, and digital signature. Click Accept in the top right corner of the window.
By choosing to Accept, you agree that the digital signature is the legally binding electronic representation of your signature and initials.

Next, the CLA Agreement will open. You must review its three pages and complete the required fields.

Click the arrows to learn more.

items.description_html: Let's take a look at the key steps that need to be taken before presenting a contribution or proposal to the OCP Community, from ensuring the necessary agreements are in place to successfully navigating the submission, review, and approval process.

• In the For the: field, input the title of your contribution project.

  • Review the entire page.

  • Click the green Next button in the top-right corner, or the black next arrow on the far right.

• Review the content of the second page.

  • Click the black next arrow again to proceed.

Review the content, then complete the four required fields:

  • By: (Authorized Signature)

  • Name: (Print Name)

  • On Behalf Of: e.g. Company Name (Highest level Bound Entity that is bound to this Agreement)

  • Date:

When all fields are filled out, select Finish in the top right corner.

Summary

By following these steps, you can ensure a smooth process for presenting and approving contributions. Proper documentation, clear communication, and alignment with OCP’s core values are essential for successful contributions to the community.

Remember to track the process closely through the Contribution Portal and stay engaged with the Steering Committee for timely feedback and approval.

blocks.body_html: You have successfully completed Step 2 and signed the CLA!
At this point, there are no more actions for you to take until the Project Lead approves your contribution abstract.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 3
Project Lead: Review Contribution Abstract

blocks.body_html: As shown by the profile icon next to Step 4, this step is assigned to the Project Lead. Their task is to review the abstract you submitted in Step 1. Once they approve the abstract, the next two steps (Steps 5 and 6) will unlock and become available for you to complete.

As shown by the profile icon next to Step 3, this step is assigned to the PL, requiring them to review the contribution abstract you submitted. Once they have completed this task, steps 4 and 5 unlock for you to proceed.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 4
Abstract Accepted! Start working on your contribution

blocks.body_html: With your abstract accepted, you can begin developing your full contribution.
Click Review on Step 4.
The side panel will open prompting you to confirm that you are using the correct contribution template.

The Contribution Templates & Agreements (opens in a new tab) link in the panel takes you to the OCP website, where you can download the official templates. Make sure to select the one that matches your contribution type to ensure that your documentation aligns with OCP standards and expectations.

Once you’ve reviewed the available templates and downloaded the correct one, return to the side panel and click Complete to move forward.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 5
Upload Specification Document for PL Review

blocks.body_html:
This step is shared between you and the PL. At this point, you're actively working on your contribution, developing your documentation using the official template and preparing a slide deck that summarizes your submission.

When you’re ready to share your draft with OCP for review, click  Review on Step 5. In the side panel select Upload Files, then attach:

These materials will be reviewed by both the PL and the SC Rep assigned to your project.

After uploading the files, hit Submit to mark the task as complete from your side. This indicates that your submission is ready for review.

Click the play icon to see this step in action.

This step will show as completed in the platform once the PL and SC Rep review the uploaded materials and provide any comments or suggestions directly within the specification document.

Even if your document still needs some refinement, you will have the opportunity to present it during a OCP Project call. The presentation slide deck must be uploaded at this stage, so scheduling can begin in advance, minimizing wait time. To schedule your presentation, please reach out to the Project Lead(s).

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 6
Acknowledge Project Group Presentation

blocks.body_html: Once the PL marks Step 5 as complete, both Steps 6 and 7 will unlock. Step 6 is an action for the PL who will review your presentation slide deck and formally acknowledge that your contribution has been presented to the OCP Project. While you do not need to take action in this step, it signifies an important milestone: your submission has now been discussed with the relevant technical community.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 7
Upload Final Project Specification and Presentation

blocks.body_html:
Step 7 is where you submit your updated versions of both the specification document and the slide deck, incorporating any changes suggested during the OCP Project presentation or by the reviewers.

By this stage, you've already presented your contribution and likely received feedback, either during the presentation or through the platform's document review process. You may have made updates to your specification document and presentation in response.

To complete this step, click Review followed by Upload Files in the side panel. Attach the final versions of your specification and slide deck, with all feedback and revisions incorporated. Hit Submit to finish.

Click the play icon to see this step in action.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 8
Accept This Contribution?

blocks.body_html: In this step, the PL reviews your updated files and, if accepted, completes Step 8 to accept your contribution on behalf of the relevant OCP Project. You have no action here, but you can track the step in the workflow.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 9
Accept This Contribution?

blocks.body_html: After the PL accepts your contribution in Step 8, your SC Rep reviews the updated specification and presentation. They can then complete Step 9 to accept it on behalf of the SC.
If at any point your submission is not accepted by the PL or SC, you’ll be asked to revise and resubmit. The steps would then need to be repeated as necessary.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 10
Acknowledge Confirmed Committee Presentation Date/Time and Meeting Link

blocks.body_html:
This step is a joint action between you and OCP Foundation Staff. At this stage, OCP Foundation Staff will propose a date and time for your official presentation to the full Steering Committee at an upcoming meeting.

This proposal will appear in your workspace. To proceed, click Review on Step 10. In the side panel, you'll see the proposed date and time for your Steering Committee presentation.

This step is a joint action between you and OCP Foundation Staff. At this stage, OCP Foundation Staff will propose a date and time for your official presentation to the full Steering Committee at an upcoming meeting.

This proposal will appear in your workspace. To proceed, click Review on Step 10.

In the side panel, you'll see the proposed date and time for your Steering Committee presentation.

If the proposed date works for you, simply click Acknowledge.
You'll then be prompted to confirm your selection again by clicking I Acknowledge in the pop-up window. Once completed, this step will be marked as done.

If the proposed date doesn't work for you, do not click Acknowledge. Instead, use the comment box at the bottom of the panel to let the OCP Foundation Staff know:

“I’m not available on that date. Please let me know the next available Steering Committee meeting date and time.”
OCP Steering Committee meetings typically occur once per month, therefore rescheduled meetings are likely to be several weeks later.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 11
Confirm Committee Presentation Completed

blocks.body_html:
Once you have presented your contribution to the Steering Committee, OCP Foundation Staff confirms the presentation in the workspace. This will launch a new workspace where the Steering Committee will review, and provide any feedback that is recommended to be incorporated into your final contribution document.

This an important milestone that signals your contribution has entered its final approval phase.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 12
Review SC Feedback with Contributor

blocks.body_html:
Once the Steering Committee presentation has been confirmed as complete, the PL reviews the SC feedback with the Contributor. The PL ensures the Contributor understands the feedback, clarifies any recommendations from the SC, and supports them in identifying where final edits or adjustments should be made to the contribution document.

This collaborative review helps ensure that all SC input is addressed before the updated specification is uploaded in Step 13.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 13
Upload Final Specification Document(s)

blocks.body_html:
If you received any feedback from the SC during your presentation, update your submission accordingly. This will be the final version that the Steering Committee votes to accept for publication and the version that will be published in the OCP Contribution Database.

Upload it by clicking Review on Step 13. In the side panel, select Upload Files, attach your updated specification, and hit Submit.

Click the arrows to view the process.
Skip this step if there are no updates (the previously uploaded version will move forward in the process).

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 14
(Optional) OCP Contribution Exclusion Period Opt-Out

blocks.body_html:
Once your contribution is accepted by the SC you have the ability to opt-out of the 30-day exclusion period that is required by the OWFa 0.9 CLA prior to publication.

If there are multiple organizations participating in the contribution, an authorized representative from each organization will need to email contributions@opencompute.org to notify OCP Foundation Staff that they are waiving the 30-day exclusion period.

If all parties agree to waive the 30-day exclusion period, then the contribution will be published as soon as it has received the majority accept vote from the Steering Committee.

To do that, click Review on Step 14. Read the opt-out statement, then click Approve if you want your contribution to be published as soon as the SC gives final approval.
To do that, click Review on Step 14.
Read the opt-out statement, then click Approve if you want your contribution to be published as soon as the SC gives final approval.
If you'd rather let the 30-day window run its course, leave this step incomplete. It's optional and won't affect the rest of your workflow.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 15
Steering Committee Decision

blocks.body_html:
Once the majority accept vote is received from the Steering Committee, the contribution moves to the final confirmation.

If your contribution has been approved for publication, OCP Foundation Staff will notify you of the result and you will receive a prompt to acknowledge.
Click Review on Step 15.
In the side panel, you'll view the decision, then hit Acknowledge to proceed.

You'll then be prompted to confirm by clicking I Acknowledge in the pop-up window.

Once completed, this step will be marked as done.
If, for any reason, you decide to withdraw your contribution at this stage, you must notify OCP Foundation Staff through the Chat Window.
This is your final opportunity to confirm or withdraw your contribution before publication.

blocks.heading_html:
Step 16
Upload to the OCP Contribution Database

blocks.body_html: In this final step, after the 30-day exclusion period has expired or all contributors have waived the opt-out period, OCP Foundation Staff uploads your contribution to the OCP Contribution Database, making it publicly accessible as an official OCP Contribution.
Congratulations! You'll be notified and able to see your listing, and share the link to this content, when your contribution has been officially uploaded and published.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

buttons.label: GO TO SUMMARY

Select an answer, then click SUBMIT.

Select all that apply, then click SUBMIT.

choices.text_html: Ask questions directly to your Project Lead.
Receive updates about step completions.

Withdraw your contribution.

blocks.feedback_correct_html: Well done! That's correct.

blocks.heading_html: You've Reached the End of the OCP Contribution Process Module!

blocks.body_html:
By now, you should have a solid understanding of what it takes to submit a contribution to the OCP Contribution Database, from the first abstract submission all the way through final publication.

Let's quickly recap what you've learned. Click the icons to uncover the key learnings.

items.description_html: How to kick off a new contribution using the OCP Contribution Hub.
What the Contributor License Agreement (CLA) is, and why it matters.
How to collaborate with Project Leads and Steering Committee members.
What steps are involved in drafting, reviewing, and presenting your contribution.
The importance of the 30-day exclusion period, and what opting out means.
How to communicate effectively using the Chat Window.
How to track progress every step of the way.

blocks.body_html: Whether you're submitting a specification, white paper, design file, or software contribution, the platform and process are designed to support you.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html: What's Next?

blocks.body_html: If you're ready to contribute, visit the OCP website and start a new submission.

buttons.label: Click Here
buttons.description_html: Click the button to access the OCP Contribution Process Welcome page.

blocks.body_html: Remember the following tips:

items.description_html: Follow the steps in order.
Ask your Project Lead if you're unsure about anything.
Use the available templates.
Keep an eye on your workspace and Chat Window for important updates.

blocks.heading_html: Thank You for Contributing to OCP!

blocks.body_html:
Your contributions help shape open, collaborative innovation across the tech industry. We appreciate your work and your voice in the OCP Community.

You can always revisit this module as a reference, or share it with colleagues who are contributing for the first time.
